Research directions

Explore a direction, then follow the papers.
Competing objectives

How do we cover the space of trade-offs?

A preference weight is a dial, but turning it evenly can leave gaps in the solutions. Geometry tells us how to explore the Pareto front.

Explore the idea

Same front. Different coverage.

Even weight increments produce uneven gaps.

An exact toy example of the spacing problem behind SURF. Both objectives are minimized.

Nested decisions

What changes when learning has an inner problem?

An outer decision changes an inner solution. My work studies the curvature, update rules, and constraints that make this learning process efficient.

Explore the idea

The bakery sets a price. The customer responds.

The shop wants profit. The customer chooses how much bread is worth buying at that price.

$3.00

Add optional constraints

No extra constraints.

Customer buys, y5 kg
Bakery profit$10.00
Preferred purchasePurchase with selected limits

At $3 per kg, the customer buys 5 kg. The bakery earns $10.

The bakery must anticipate the customer’s response when choosing its price.

About this illustrative model

Without extra limits, the customer prefers 8 − x kg. This maximizes their modeled satisfaction minus the price paid. Bread costs the shop $1 per kg, so profit is (x − 1)y.

A budget limits spending: xy ≤ 12. Stock limits the amount bought: y ≤ 3. These are teaching assumptions, not data from a paper.

Behind the work

Liuyuan Jiang

I am a PhD student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Rochester, advised by Prof. Lisha Chen. Previously, I was a PhD student at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, advised by Prof. Tianyi Chen.

I study how optimization shapes learning: navigating competing objectives, solving nested problems, and understanding model behavior.

Each project page combines an accessible explanation with the method, results, and technical scope. Video narration and storyboards have their own pages.
